faults.name: Open or closed stance

faults.name: Head lurch
faults.description: The head makes a sudden, jerky movement toward the target during the transition at the top, disrupting balance and eye contact with the ball.

faults.name: Forearm roll

faults.name: Head dives

faults.name: Shoulders vs feet

faults.description: An S-posture characterized by a locked, rigid spine with excessive arch in the lower back, leading to tension and restricted rotation.

faults.name: Loss of posture
faults.description: The golfer stands up or loses their initial spine angle during the backswing, requiring a downward compensation to strike the ball.

faults.name: Forearm roll
faults.description: The forearms rotate excessively during the initial movement, fanning the clubface open and requiring severe compensation later in the swing.

faults.name: Head lurch
faults.description: The head makes a sudden, jerky movement toward the target during the transition at the top, disrupting balance and eye contact with the ball.

faults.name: Hands flip
faults.description: The wrists actively break down and flip the clubhead past the hands during the downswing prior to impact, adding loft and reducing compression.

faults.name: Loss of lag
faults.description: The angle between the lead forearm and the clubshaft is cast or released immediately from the top of the swing, bleeding power before impact.

faults.name: Hands flip
faults.description: The wrists actively break down and flip the clubhead past the hands during the downswing prior to impact, adding loft and reducing compression.

faults.name: Head backs away
faults.description: The head moves up and away from the ball during the downswing, often as a compensation for early extension.
